requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`:

- **First result carries `instructions`, even when empty.** The first successful `search_text` for "absent" returns no matches. The test asserts that `instructions` is a string. It also asserts that a fresh session's first search ("hit") and a peer session's first search both carry the same `instructions`. This covers "each conversation".
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** Under `default-languages`, the peer session's first call is `search_structure`. It returns `matches == []` and carries `instructions` equal to the text-search value. A later `search_text` on that peer session has no `instructions`.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** The session's first call is an invalid `search_text` pattern "(", which errors. The next successful search, the empty one, still carries `instructions`.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.** `get_next_page` on the fresh session's first result has no `instructions`. A later `search_text` on the peer session has none. A search made after the first one was closed has none (`first.get("instructions").is_none()`). The page delivered by `get_next_page` after the file changed has none (`second`).
- **The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags go in `used`.** The test checks that the text contains these phrases:
  - "Before submitting, close every delivered search page"
  - "finish_search"
  - "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read"
  - "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result"
  - "without reading more source"

  Those phrases match the cited `finish_search.mcp.description` content. The exact wording is the separate `.content` requirement and is outside this assessment.

I read `Pages::search` in `pages.rs` to check one point: whether a failed structural search could consume the first-search state. `first_search` is `self.searches.is_empty()` and a search is recorded only on successful delivery. Failures therefore take the same path for both tools, so the text-search failure test is sufficient. The "instructions only on the first page" behaviour (`index == 0`) is also exercised by the continuation-page assertions. I found no gap.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
